vulnerable_code:
@router.post("/sso/saml/acs")
async def saml_global_acs(
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)
):
    form_data = await request.form()
    relay_state = form_data.get("RelayState", "")
    target_account_id = None
    if relay_state and "account_id=" in relay_state:
        target_account_id = relay_state.split("account_id=")[1].split("&")[0]

    req_data = await prepare_fastapi_request_for_saml(request)
    auth = OneLogin_Saml2_Auth(req_data, get_global_saml_settings())
    auth.process_response()

    if auth.get_errors():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="SAML verification failed")

    user_email = auth.get_nameid()
    user = await db.scalar(select(User).where(User.email == user_email))
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")

    bound_account = target_account_id or user.default_account_id
    token = issue_account_scoped_token(user.id, bound_account)
    return {"token": token, "active_account_id": bound_account}
diagnosis: The global SAML ACS endpoint parses target_account_id directly out of the client-controlled RelayState form parameter and issues an account-scoped token for that account ID. It never verifies that the authenticated user has membership or authorization in target_account_id, allowing any user authenticated via SSO to bind their session to arbitrary corporate accounts.
